protections: A GitHub App user's team group principals are exactly the teams recorded for that user in the installation data (gitHubAppData.members[username].orgs[org]), resolved against that org's own teams map - not every team of every org the user appears in (pkg/auth/providers/githubapp/github_data.go:89-90,117-130).

Group principals used to authorize a request are re-derived from the provider and not taken from previously persisted copies (UserAttribute.GroupPrincipals written at pkg/auth/providerrefresh/refresher.go:287, legacy token GroupPrincipals at pkg/apis/management.cattle.io/v3/authn_types.go:81) - pkg/auth/requests/authenticate.go:206-226.
A refresh that fails does not leave the old (over-inclusive) principal set in force: the refreshed set replaces the stored one - pkg/auth/providerrefresh/refresher.go:260-288.

The admin-facing surface must stay membership-blind: team discovery for granting (SearchPrincipals/team search) must return every team of every installed org regardless of who is a member (pkg/auth/providers/githubapp/github_data.go:147-159, pkg/auth/providers/githubapp/githubapp_provider.go:257-266).

masking: Fixing T1 turns the repo's own tests red: pkg/auth/providers/githubapp/github_data_test.go:218-277 asserts admin-team is returned for test-user, and the fixture at github_data_test.go:49 keeps the dangling 'example' slug in the member map, so a solver who treats the pinned tests as the spec re-introduces the bug.

T2 is invisible until T1 is fixed: the refresh the migration would trigger re-runs listTeamsForUser, so adding the startup migration while leaving the computation alone rewrites exactly the same over-inclusive principals.

T3 only becomes the visible cause once T1 is fixed: with the computation correct, the only way the stale over-inclusive set survives a refresh is refresher.go:269-272 retaining it on error, so a fix for T1 hides T3 behind a passing login test.

conflicts.what: The natural place to enforce membership is the shared producer or the search helper: filtering gatherDataForInstallation (github_data.go:321-345) or searchTeams (github_data.go:147-159) by membership closes T1 but leaves admins unable to find or grant a team in SearchPrincipals (githubapp_provider.go:257-266), and filtering the data at collection time also starves listTeams/listOrgs tests. The guard has to be inside listTeamsForUser only.

The startup bulk re-derivation that T2 needs is a no-op for any user whose refresh lands in T3's error branch: refresher.go:269-272 puts the old over-inclusive principals back and :287 persists them, so a T2-only fix silently keeps the vulnerable state whenever GitHub is slow or a token cannot be minted.

The obvious hardening for T4 (never use the token's stored principals) also refuses the shape other providers rely on when their UserAttribute entry is absent (authenticate.go:219-226 also serves tokens with an empty provider field, and usermanager.go:495-498 mirrors it), so a blanket rule breaks legitimate legacy logins while a provider-scoped rule leaves the fallback in place for every other provider.

fairness_risks: Must-keep-working: team search and principal selection must stay membership-blind (github_data.go:147-159, githubapp_provider.go:257-266) or admins can no longer grant team principals; a security rule phrased as 'never return teams a user is not in' would contradict it if applied to the search surface.

Must-keep-working: a legitimate member must still get their real team principals, otherwise restricted-mode login fails at githubapp_provider.go:172-183 (testAllowedPrincipals is only extended with the user principal when test=true).

Refused input shape a legitimate use needs: a membership slice naming a slug that org.teams does not contain (github_data_test.go:27) is legitimate GitHub data (a team the installation token cannot see); skipping it is required, rejecting it or emitting a zero-ID account is not.

In unrestricted mode CheckAccess returns true before any principal is examined (usermanager.go:186-188), so a rule written against CheckAccess rather than the principal set is untestable in the default access mode; hidden tests must run required/restricted or assert on the principal set.

Removing the legacy token-group-principal fallback (authenticate.go:219-226) would change behaviour for tokens with an empty provider field, a shape older deployments still present; a rule that 'token group principals must never be trusted' refuses input legitimate old tokens rely on.

The pinned tests encode the vulnerable expectation (github_data_test.go:218-277), so any grading rule of the form 'existing project tests must pass' contradicts the fix; the fix necessarily updates that subtest.

design.why: T1 is the anchor the report names (easy for both models, keeps the task solvable and gives the stack its landing point) and carries T1b's M8 shapes - the same-slug-in-two-orgs resolution and the dangling-slug skip - which a rushed rewrite gets wrong. T5 is the mimo-type coupled value: the same producer feeds a deliberately membership-blind search surface, so over-hardening at gatherDataForInstallation or searchTeams breaks team grants while the login still succeeds. T2 is a deepseek-type protected-absent site in another layer with a strong reason to dismiss (the 3600s max-age refresh 'covers it'), and it is exactly the stored state that request authorization reads. T3 supplies a second deepseek-type at distance 1 whose dismissal ('resilience on transient errors') is different again, and it also degrades T2's fix. The four have four different dismissals (org filter looks like membership / search is meant to be broad / scheduled refresh covers stored copies / errors must not lock users out) and three different layers (provider expansion, data producer, stored-state refresh), which is what makes the stack resist a single-judgement solve. T4 is documented but excluded from the design: at the pinned commit every login writes a provider entry (usermanager.go:397), so the fallback is only reachable through a state no in-repo path creates, which makes it unfair to grade; T2 also needs the builder to accept a startup-path or new-API test (see unverified), and if it does not, T1+T1b/T5/T3 is still a valid 3-trap stack.

unverified: Fix commit contents are not readable from this worktree (only the pinned tree was in scope), so the claims attributed to fix.diff - the new pkg/data/management/githubapp_refresh_users.go, the TriggerAllUserRefresh package wrapper at what the screener calls fix.diff:13-21, the mcm.Start call, and the second commit's JSON MergePatch repair of a typed AuthConfig Update - come from the screener record and were not confirmed here.

Whether hidden behavioural tests can score T2: the protection lives in code that does not exist at the pinned commit (no RefreshGitHubAppUsersOnce; grep finds no package-level TriggerAllUserRefresh), so a test cannot name it unless the task builder fixes the API or drives mcm.Start. Without that, T2 is a design fact but not a gradeable trap.

Whether T4 is reachable in production: no pinned path mints a githubapp token whose UserAttribute lacks a githubapp GroupPrincipals entry, so its protection_state 'weak' is a code-shape judgement, not an observed route.
present_in_latest for T3 and T4 was not checked: only the pinned tree was available and the input reports no latest release.
Repository size in MB was not measured; the tree has no vendor directory and spans multiple Go modules plus a web UI, so it is not a tiny repo.

Regression tests: pkg/auth/providers/githubapp/github_data_test.go:218-277 still expects the buggy result and pkg/auth/providers/githubapp/githubapp_client_test.go:202,249 exercise getTeamsForUser against a fake server with no per-team member lists (fake_github_server_test.go:124-205 defines teams without members), so whether those client tests also encode the over-inclusive result could not be settled.

The screener's O1=3 entry-point count (public login, testAndApply, RefetchGroupPrincipals) was not re-derived: all three funnel into listTeamsForUser and are one guard, which is why they are grouped with T1 rather than counted separately.
